question: Consider the pytest test `optuna_qa/transform_transform_search_space_s3_state/files/testcase.py::TestTransformSearchSpaceState::test_transform_mixed_search_space` (test class `TestTransformSearchSpaceState`, its single test method `test_transform_mixed_search_space`). During this test the function `optuna._transform._transform_search_space` (defined in `optuna/_transform.py`, lines 175-243) is invoked exactly once. Report the complete ordered history of values bound to the local variable `bds` during that invocation. A new history entry is produced every time an assignment statement whose target is `bds` finishes executing (the multi-line `bds = (...)` statements in the FloatDistribution and IntDistribution branches, which start on lines 209, 214, 221, 226). Every executed assignment counts as its own entry, even if the new value equals the previous one (no deduplication); entries are in chronological execution order. Iterations that handle a CategoricalDistribution do not assign `bds` and therefore produce no entry. Answer as JSON of the form {"value_history": [{"step": <int>, "value": <str>}, ...]} where `step` is the 1-based position of the assignment in chronological order (1, 2, 3, ...) and `value` is the Python `repr()` of the value of `bds` immediately after that assignment completes, i.e. the repr of the whole tuple exactly as Python prints it (for example a tuple of two floats looks like `(-1.25, 3.0)`, with full shortest round-trip float digits as produced by `repr(float)`, a space after the comma, and no numpy wrappers if the elements are plain Python floats).
